text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH

- Turkish judges and prosecutors showed their loyalty to secularism by turning out in large numbers for a military briefing on Islamic fundementalism, despite threats by the Islamist justice minister.
- The first state wheat purchase price in southern Turkey is one or two thousand lira below the price previously announced.
MILLIYET
- The army general staff named six Islamist companies they said were aiding Islamic fundementalism.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan says civil servant salaries will be linked to inflation from June.
HURRIYET
- The Islamist-led government has given permission to Islamic banks to operate on the Istanbul gold exchange.
YENI YUZYIL
- Tansu Ciller, leader of the coalition government's conservative wing, has agreed on early elections within the current electorate system.
- British holidaymakers have not cancelled holidays in Turkey despite bomb threats on tourist sites by Kurdish rebels.
RADIKAL
- State Minister Salim Ensarioglu who allegedly has two wives is appointed acting minister responsible for women and the family.
DUNYA
- The Treasury has changed the rules of Istanbul gold exchange to accept foreign based members.
- A parliamentary commission agreed on a law gathering all laws and regulations concerning the customs union under one law.
ZAMAN
- Turkish troops have inflicted heavy damage on Kurdish guerillas so far in 1997, killing 1,079 rebels in southeast Turkey and 2,500 in northern Iraq.
CUMHURIYET
- There is no sign from Erbakan of an early handover of the premiership to his coaliton partner Ciller.
